newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Private sector credit growth slowed only marginally to 16.39 percent in June compared to May's 16.65 percent -- delivering a setback to market hopes for an interest rate cut.
- The defence force had failed to timeously or properly account for aircraft components worth 6.1 billion rand, according to an investigation by the Auditor-General.
- Deutsche Morgan Grenfell has been appointed as transaction adviser for the partial privatisation of the 2.5 billion rand Airports Company, which should be completed by March next year.

- The gold mines serviced by Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd reported one of their worst aggregate quarterly performances in the June quarter, swinging to a taxed cash loss of 41 million rand from a 55 million rand taxed profit in the March quarter.
- The involvement of private sector managers in running the reconstruction and development programme had helped to produce a massive rise in expenditure, the finance department said.
- The environmental affairs and tourism department has proposed an international departure tax of about $15 payable by every person leaving South Africa, as a means of funding the tourism promotion.
- The government intends to privatise 100 percent of PX, Transnet's loss-making parcel delivery subsidiary, and road transport operator Autonet, Transport Minister Mac Maharaj said.
- Southern Asset Management said it had executed a two billion rand portfolio trade in a deal that ranks as the largest single trade ever on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
- Randgold has made an urgent plea to the government for assistance in pumping water from two of its mines.
- Retail sales are expected to flatten in the third quarter, according to Stellenbosch university's Bureau for Economic Research.
- Police fraud units and the Office for Serious Economic Offences are investigating white-collar fraud totalling more than 15 billion rand.
- Gauteng police, assisted by private industry, have seized large quantities of counterfeit famous-name goods in a series of raids aimed at clamping down on informal traders and their suppliers.
